offence_severity: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and also liable to fine
physical_harm: Injuries sustained on her person due to beating
number_of_offences: Charges framed under Sections 342, 324, 323 and 354 of the IPC; charge under Section 366 IPC was dismissed
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the accused forcibly took the appellant to his house, beat her, and that the act of pulling her out of the car was witnessed by a watchman.
witness_credibility: The court expressed skepticism about the appellant's later statement regarding molestation, noting that the FIR was lodged five days after the incident with due deliberation, and the explanation for the delay in mentioning molestation was not convincing.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 06.09.2003; Trial judgment: 04.07.2007; High Court decision: 06.05.2013; Supreme Court decision: 24.04.2018
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Siddharth Luthra, Robin Jaisinghani, Vikas Mehta, Vijay Gandhi, Samir Chaudhary, Ms. Purnima Raj, Ms. Anushree Menon; Counsel for the State: Mahesh Jethmalani, Nishant R. Katneshwarkar, Anand, Rahul M, Ms. R. N. Reddy, Dr. Sushil Balwada
investigation_status: FIR registered on 12.09.2003; Charge sheet filed on 30.03.2004; Trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Discharge order dated 04.07.2007; High Court: Dismissed writ petition dated 06.05.2013; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed on 24.04.2018
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant made out a case of being molested by Respondent No. 2 and that the allegations of abduction and forced taking to his house were sufficient to charge him under Section 366 of the IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR was lodged five days after the incident with due deliberation, and the later statement about molestation was an afterthought, not inspired by embarrassment. They also relied on precedents to show that the High Court and Sessions Court orders should not be interfered with.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for an offence under Section 366 of the IPC, it must be proved that the accused abducted the woman with the intent to compel her to marry or to force/seduce her to illicit intercourse.
precedent_relied_upon: Cref Finance Ltd. v. Shree Shanthi Homes (P) Ltd. and Another (2005) 7 SCC 467; Dharam Pal and Others v. State of Haryana and Another (2014) 3 SCC 306
